answer: Proof-of-replication limits Sybils in an agent market trading karst drainage, copper assay, and ledge survey feeds. Each node encodes a unique replica bound to its public key via slow sequential hashing over a depth-robust graph, then answers random Merkle audits faster than re-encoding allows. Every fake identity thus incurs verifiable physical disk storage and sealing work that cannot be shared across accounts. Yet operators renting bulk storage clusters can still sustain large node fleets.
